All 11 phases closed COMPLETED or COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS; the sole residual exclusion is a pre-existing, out-of-scope C15 paper-anchor gap recorded since Phase 1.

memory_candidates.content: When a Lake package's lintDriver-based `lake lint` gate (Batteries `runLinter`) cannot narrow which env_linters run -- its CLI has no linter-selection flag, always running every registered `@[env_linter]` check -- the standard Batteries/Mathlib resolution is `scripts/nolints.json`: generate it via `lake exe runLinter --update <module>`, and it is read unconditionally on every subsequent run, filtering grandfathered (linter, declaration) pairs out of the failing set before judging pass/fail. This achieves 'CI fails only on genuinely new violations' without narrowing the linter set at all -- a strictly stronger regression gate than picking a small blocking subset. Caveat when regenerating: the run that performs `--update` still judges its own pass/fail against the PRE-update grandfather set (the write is a side effect), so it will still exit nonzero on that invocation even though the file it just wrote will make the NEXT plain run pass.

Lean's `dupNamespace` linter is a Lean-core/Mathlib text linter (`Mathlib.Tactic.Linter.Lint`, `register_option linter.dupNamespace`), architecturally distinct from Batteries' `@[env_linter]` family (`simpNF`, `docBlame`, `unusedArguments`, etc.) that `lake exe runLinter`/`lintDriver` checks -- it never appears in that tool's output regardless of its true count. The only way to isolate it via the real linter is `lake lint --builtin-only --lint-only .dupNamespace`, which forces Lake to rebuild the ENTIRE default target under different linter options on every invocation (confirmed costly, ~10 minutes on a mid-size project, and a real OOM risk) -- unsuitable for a routinely-run local gate. A cheap, validated alternative for a REPORTING-ONLY check: detect it textually. Track `namespace`/`section`/`end` nesting in a single pass; flag any `structure`/`inductive`/`def`/`abbrev`/`theorem`/`instance`/`class` whose declared name repeats a currently-open namespace segment. For a `structure`/`class` specifically, the real linter also flags every auto-generated field projection and the implicit `.mk` constructor (not just the type's own declaration line) -- omitting this undercounts by roughly the field count. Watch for `_root_.A.B.C`-qualified declarations, which escape every currently-open namespace and must NOT be combined with the open-namespace stack (a common false-positive source). Validated to reproduce the real linter's exact finding count and line numbers on a real codebase (14/14) once both refinements were applied; runs in well under a second over a ~500-file tree.

A reporting-only heuristic check with an authored numeric floor (e.g. 'docstring coverage must be >= 90%') should, when a faithful measurement lands under the floor, STOP and escalate rather than either (a) silently landing a failing/misleading check, or (b) unilaterally adjusting the measurement methodology to clear the floor. If a documented, already-anticipated blind spot in the heuristic (not a new discovery) plausibly explains the shortfall, escalating with that evidence lets the floor's owner authorize a specific, narrow refinement -- which should then be applied exactly ONCE as a precisely-specified rule (never iterated toward a target number), with both the original and refined figures reported side by side so a future reader can see the number moved because the definition changed, not because reality changed. Sanity-check the refinement in BOTH directions before trusting it: verify the original under-count's samples are genuinely covered by the blind spot, AND verify the refinement's own newly-credited samples are genuinely covered (a naive refinement can easily over-credit -- e.g. a section-comment-based rule with no 'ends at the next explicitly-documented item' boundary condition let credit leak hundreds of lines into unrelated content in one real case).
